ns2:course.label: Bioengineering Senior Design
ns2:course.description: Students perform market research and explore entrepreneurship in bioengineering resulting in the design of a device or process; practice problem identification and analyze solutions for real-world problems from the perspective of value added for end-users; use principles of design, engineering analysis, and customer discovery. This course emphasizes effective teamwork and technical communication; integrates intellectual property, United States Food and Drug Administration Quality System Regulation and Design Controls, human-centered design, FDA regulation, professionalism, and ethics. 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. Prerequisite: BIOE 302, BIOE 303, BIOE 414, BIOE 415. Restricted to students in the Bioengineering Bachelor of Science program.
